summary: Iteration 12 — Synced lyrics via LRCLIB.net + LyricsDisplay HUD. BACKEND: created /app/backend/tests/test_iter12_lyrics.py (14 tests) covering GET /api/tracks/lyrics (real LRCLIB upstream — Coldplay/Yellow returns 38 synced lines, Above & Beyond/Sun & Moon returns synced lyrics found=true), Mongo positive AND negative cache (cached:true on repeat for both hit and miss), refresh=1 bypass, empty-artist+title short-circuit (no upstream call), POST /api/admin/tracks/lyrics auth (401 unauth), manual LRC parsing happy-path, 400 on empty artist+title, multi-timestamp lines, section-label filtering, and three direct parse_lrc unit tests. 12/14 PASS, 2 FAIL — both are the SAME bug: the LRC parser regex eagerly matches the first timestamp and greedily captures the rest of the line (including a second [mm:ss.xx] prefix) into the `text` group, so multi-timestamp lines like `[00:01.00][00:02.50]Same` produce ONE entry `{time:1.0, text:'[00:02.50]Same'}` instead of the spec-required TWO entries at 1.0s and 2.5s with text 'Same'. The else/fallback branch in lyrics_service.parse_lrc that handles multi-timestamp prefixes IS NEVER REACHED for typical LRC because the primary regex already 'succeeds' on the first prefix. Verified by running `parse_lrc('[00:01.00][00:02.50]Same\n[00:10.00]Other')` directly in-process → output [{time:1.0, text:'[00:02.50]Same'}, {time:10.0, text:'Other'}]. Full pytest regression: 125 passed + 8 skipped (Redis only) + 2 failed in 25.85s across 10 test files (135 total, +14 vs iter11 baseline). Phase2 Redis tests still skipped (expected). FRONTEND: walked through the full LyricsDisplay HUD on /mix/3f4de4bc-5f23-4f56-96dc-25245a845083 (planted Coldplay-Yellow @ 0s/87BPM/6A and Above & Beyond-Sun & Moon @ 60s/132BPM/8A via PATCH, restored to MIDNIGHT DRIVE VOL.01 demo tracks after testing). VERIFIED: data-testid lyrics-display renders BETWEEN the dual waveform and the DECK B NEXT row (correct slotting); lyric-prev, lyric-current, lyric-next all present and react to window.__mixdeckAudio.currentTime; pre-vocals state shows data-testid='lyrics-intro' with '♪ vocals in 36s' countdown; at currentTime=38 (past Yellow's first lyric at 35.66s) lyric-current shows EXACTLY 'Look at the stars' (spec-required string); offset-toggle button opens lyrics-offset-panel with lyrics-offset-slider (range -5..+5 step 0.1), changing slider to 2.5 immediately persists localStorage 'mixdeck_lyric_offsets' = '{"Coldplay|Yellow":2.5}'; lyrics-hide button hides the panel, shows lyrics-show restore handle, and writes localStorage 'mixdeck_lyrics_hidden' = '1'; clicking restore brings panel back and flips key to '0'. The // LYRICS source label shows '· lrclib' confirming end-to-end LRCLIB → backend → frontend flow. ONE FRONTEND ITEM NOT FULLY VERIFIED: cue-boundary refetch when crossing into Sun & Moon at currentTime=70. Setting window.__mixdeckAudio.currentTime=70 did not appear to swap the active track display (DECK A LIVE still read Yellow). Suspect this is either (a) the audio source clamped the seek (the demo mix audio_url is shorter than 70s and seek silently clamps), or (b) the activeTrack derivation in DjConsole doesn't switch on currentTime>=track.start_seconds when the audio can't actually reach that time. The lyric component itself correctly fetches on artist/title prop change (verified by initial mount triggering /api/tracks/lyrics?artist=Coldplay&title=Yellow), so the wiring is sound — only the cue-boundary trigger itself is unverified.

critical.issue: Multi-timestamp LRC lines are parsed wrong. `[00:01.00][00:02.50]Same` produces ONE entry {time:1.0, text:'[00:02.50]Same'} instead of TWO entries (time:1.0 'Same' and time:2.5 'Same'). RCA: LRC_LINE_RE = r'^\[(\d+):(\d+)(?:[.:](\d+))?\](.*)$' matches greedily on the first timestamp and the trailing `.*` swallows the second timestamp prefix. The intended fallback branch (line 56-63) that uses re.findall to extract all prefixes is therefore dead code for typical input. Fix: either (a) check if the captured `text` still starts with `[` (a leftover timestamp) and route to the multi-ts branch, or (b) make LRC_LINE_RE only match when there is NOT another `[` after `]` (negative lookahead), or (c) always run re.findall on the line for all `\[mm:ss(\.xx)?\]` prefixes and treat everything after the last `]` as the text. Option (c) is cleanest. Real LRCLIB tracks DO contain multi-timestamp lines (used to deduplicate repeated choruses), so this likely affects some synced lyrics in production silently — currently each repeated line collapses to a single first-occurrence entry plus orphan '[…]Text' entries that display the literal bracket prefix to users.

integration_issues.flow: Cue-boundary track switch on currentTime crossing
integration_issues.issue: Seeking window.__mixdeckAudio.currentTime to 70s (10s past the Sun & Moon track start at 60s) did NOT visibly update the DECK A LIVE label or the lyric content from Yellow → Sun & Moon. Likely caused by the demo mix's audio source duration clamping the seek, but worth E1 verifying that DjConsole's active-track derivation is purely time-based (currentTime comparison) and not gated by audio.readyState/audio.duration. Note: track-change lyrics refetch IS wired (the useEffect on [artist, title] in LyricsDisplay.jsx fires correctly when the activeTrack prop changes — verified at initial mount), so the issue (if any) is upstream in DjConsole's currentTrack computation, not in LyricsDisplay itself.

action_items: FIX lyrics_service.parse_lrc multi-timestamp bug. Recommended fix: replace the current if/else regex flow with a unified approach — `tags = re.findall(r'\[(\d+):(\d+)(?:[.:](\d+))?\]', line)`; `text = re.sub(r'^(?:\[\d+:\d+(?:[.:]\d+)?\])+', '', line).strip()`; then emit one {time, text} per tag. This collapses both branches into one and correctly handles 1, 2, or N timestamp prefixes. The existing section-label filter (`out = [i for i in out if not i['text'].lower().startswith(('ti:','ar:',...))]`) keeps working unchanged.

Verify DjConsole.jsx activeTrack derivation is time-only (not gated by audio readyState). Easiest check: when the user seeks past a cue point on a short-audio demo mix, the deck header should still update even if the audio element can't actually play that timestamp.
OPTIONAL: add a JSON-schema-style contract test that parse_lrc never emits text starting with `[`. That would have caught this regression.
critical_code_review_comments: lyrics_service.parse_lrc is the highest-impact issue this iteration — the regex LRC_LINE_RE is too greedy on the trailing `.*` group, so the carefully-written multi-timestamp fallback branch never executes for real input. The same code reads correctly on first glance, which is why it shipped. Add a parser-only test suite (test_lyrics_parser.py) with ~10 LRC corner cases (multi-ts, ID3 metadata lines like [ti:Yellow], section labels [Verse 1], empty lines, lines without text, BOM, CR-LF, very small fractional ms like [00:01.5] etc).

Negative-cache key in _cache_key buckets by `duration // 5` which is good for fuzzy matching, BUT the special case duration=None maps to 0//5 = 0 — meaning ALL no-duration lookups share the same bucket regardless of artist+title (artist|title still differs so it's still safe). Just noting the bucket key is fine as long as artist+title normalization stays stable.

lookup_lyrics() does upsert on EVERY cold lookup (cache miss). For a public unauthenticated endpoint this is fine, but consider adding a TTL on the negative-cache entries (e.g. retry upstream after 7 days) so that LRCLIB additions for newly-popular tracks eventually get picked up without manual /refresh=1.

/api/tracks/lyrics is unauthenticated and proxies to LRCLIB. It is now an open relay against LRCLIB rate-limited by however quickly attackers can make requests. Cache mitigates this, but for safety add per-IP simple rate limiting (e.g. 30 req/min) at the FastAPI level or in middleware. Not a blocker, but worth noting.

LyricsDisplay.jsx state machine renders correctly through 5 states (loading, no-lyrics, plain-only, intro/countdown, current). The binary search for current lyric on every render is O(log N) which is fine for typical N≤80 LRC lines.

The activeTrack-switch lyrics-refetch logic relies entirely on the (artist, title) tuple. If two consecutive tracks happen to have the same title/artist (unlikely but possible — extended/radio edit) the useEffect won't refire. Consider keying on track.index instead.

rca of the issue: lyrics_service.py:42-66 — LRC_LINE_RE = r'^\[(\d+):(\d+)(?:[.:](\d+))?\](.*)$' is greedy on group 4 (text). For input '[00:01.00][00:02.50]Same', the regex matches on the first '[00:01.00]' prefix and assigns text='[00:02.50]Same'. So the if-not-match fallback (lines 55-63) that calls re.findall to extract all timestamps NEVER fires for valid multi-prefix LRC lines. Result: spec-required behavior 'multi-timestamp lines like [00:01.00][00:02.50]Same text should produce 2 entries' is broken. Fix unified-approach: `tags = re.findall(r'\[(\d+):(\d+)(?:[.:](\d+))?\]', line); if not tags: continue; text = re.sub(r'^(?:\[\d+:\d+(?:[.:]\d+)?\])+', '', line).strip(); for mins, secs, frac in tags: t = ...; out.append({'time': round(t,3), 'text': text})`. Reproduction: `from lyrics_service import parse_lrc; print(parse_lrc('[00:01.00][00:02.50]Same\n[00:10.00]Other'))` → currently `[{'time':1.0,'text':'[00:02.50]Same'},{'time':10.0,'text':'Other'}]`; expected `[{'time':1.0,'text':'Same'},{'time':2.5,'text':'Same'},{'time':10.0,'text':'Other'}]`.
